headline: CISA revealed that Iran-linked hackers probed more than 100 internet-exposed U.S. water systems in July as the Treasury layered fresh sanctions on the same actors.

emerging_trends.text: Phishing-as-a-service crews now rent AI voice agents that call theft victims posing as Apple Support, and AnonyMousKIT's operators built a reseller supply chain of 506 domains and 168 storefront brands to strip Activation Lock from stolen iPhones.

Nation-state pressure is landing squarely on utilities, with CISA counting over 100 internet-exposed water systems probed in a single month and the Treasury sanctioning the Iranian actors behind the intrusions.

emerging_trends.text: Chipmakers and cloud vendors are racing to standardize trust for autonomous software, with AMD, Intel, Microsoft, and OPAQUE handing the TRACE runtime-attestation specification to the Linux Foundation to produce hardware-backed evidence for AI agents.

topics.title: Phishing-as-a-Service Kits Automate Credential Theft
topics.latest_developments: SOCRadar unraveled AnonyMousKIT's reseller supply chain of 506 domains and 168 storefront brands after basic coding errors exposed its production logs, while Dark Reading detailed NovaCookies, an adversary-in-the-middle kit renting Microsoft 365 session theft for $320 a month, and Zimperium flagged fake recruiters using browser-in-the-browser lures to harvest corporate passwords.
topics.summary: Rentable phishing platforms lower the bar for credential and session theft. AnonyMousKIT uses rented AI voice agents to call iPhone theft victims posing as Apple Support and pull passcodes needed to remove Activation Lock, NovaCookies steals live M365 sessions past MFA, and recruitment scams target enterprise logins on mobile. Enforce phishing-resistant authentication and monitor for session-token abuse.

topics.title: Max-Severity Flaws in Ubiquiti, Kaltura, Adobe, and Nvidia
topics.latest_developments: Ubiquiti patched three maximum-severity bugs that remote attackers can exploit without privileges, the CERT Coordination Center disclosed two unpatched Kaltura mwEmbed deserialization flaws, CVE-2026-19913 and CVE-2026-19912, that permit unauthenticated file reads and code execution, and Adobe and Nvidia each shipped advisories fixing critical vulnerabilities.
topics.summary: A fresh wave of high-impact flaws spans network gear, video players, and creative and GPU software. The Kaltura mwEmbedLoader.php bugs remain unpatched and let remote attackers read arbitrary files and run code. Patch Ubiquiti, Adobe, and Nvidia immediately, and restrict access to exposed Kaltura players until a fix ships.

sources.title: Ubiquiti patches three max severity security vulnerabilities

topics.title: Flock Surveillance Draws Felony Charges and Denials
topics.latest_developments: Police devised sting operations using 3D-printed decoy Flock cameras and charged a man with three felonies for breaking one, while 404 Media reported that Flock Chief Executive Garrett Langley told officers its earlier story about police tracking a woman who self-administered an abortion was false.
topics.summary: Flock's automated license-plate-reader network is generating legal and political friction as departments protect the cameras with decoys and sting charges and the company disputes reporting on abusive queries. Separately, ICE is seeking a federal contractor to handle national voter registration and history files it frames as fraud detection.

topics.title: Iran-Linked Hackers Probe U.S. Water Systems
topics.latest_developments: CISA disclosed that attackers targeted more than 100 internet-exposed water systems during July, tied the activity to Iran-linked actors, and published guidance on cutting internet exposure days after the Treasury's fresh sanctions.
topics.summary: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned Iranian cyber actors for critical-infrastructure breaches, and CISA now urges water utilities to pull human-machine interfaces and controllers off the public internet. Operators should segment operational-technology networks and enforce strong authentication.

sources.title: CISA: Over 100 Internet-Exposed Water Systems Targeted in July Cyberattacks

topics.title: TRACE Standardizes AI Agent Attestation
topics.latest_developments: The Linux Foundation took governance of TRACE, a hardware-backed runtime-evidence specification contributed by OPAQUE and built with AMD, Intel, Microsoft, and the Technology Innovation Institute, to create a standard evidence layer for autonomous AI agents and confidential workloads.
topics.summary: TRACE, short for Trust, Runtime Attestation and Compliance Evidence, aims to give organizations verifiable governance records as they deploy increasingly autonomous agents and open-weight models. The open standard lands as vendors race to secure agent behavior, alongside NVIDIA's SkillSpector scanner for AI agent skills.

sources.title: Linux Foundation takes on TRACE, a hardware-backed runtime evidence specification for AI agents
Linux Foundation to Govern TRACE, an Open Standard for AI Runtime Attestation

topics.title: SLEEPWALKER Packet-Triggered Windows Backdoor
topics.latest_developments: An independent malware researcher documented SLEEPWALKER, a previously unreported Windows backdoor that lies inert in memory until a specifically crafted network packet arrives, then executes commands written in its own 23-instruction language.
topics.summary: SLEEPWALKER is an unsigned 64-bit Windows DLL of 59,904 bytes built to be side-loaded into a legitimate process, where it waits for a trigger packet before running its custom bytecode. Its packet-gated dormancy defeats sandbox timers and network scanning, so defenders should hunt for suspicious side-loading and unexpected listening behavior.

sources.title: New SLEEPWALKER Backdoor Waits for One Crafted Packet, Then Runs Its Own Bytecode
